content.content:
1	"""Core schema inference and validation logic.
2	
3	A schema is a tree of nodes. Object nodes carry a mapping of field name to
4	field entry; each field entry records the set of observed types, how many
5	records carried the field, how many records were seen at that level, and
6	whether the field is optional. Array nodes merge their element types.
7	
8	Inference is a streaming fold: records are folded one at a time and never
9	retained, so peak memory tracks the size of the statistics tree, not the
10	number of records. The tree itself can be bounded with two resource limits
11	given to ``Lens``: ``max_fields`` caps how many field entries one object
12	node tracks exactly (further distinct names fold into a shared overflow
13	entry kept under the node's ``"overflow"`` key), and ``max_depth`` caps how
14	deep object and array nodes are tracked (deeper subtrees collapse into
15	summary nodes that keep only counts and element kinds). Every statistic
16	that has been approximated is flagged with ``"approximate": true`` in the
17	schema tree and listed under the ``"approximate"`` key of ``Lens.stats``,
18	so precision loss is always visible and never silent. With no limits (the
19	default) no approximation is ever triggered and the folded schema is
20	exactly the schema produced by folding every record in one pass. The field
21	cap is also enforced after two batches are merged, so a merged object node
22	can never hold more exact field entries than the cap even when the two
23	batches named disjoint sets; the excess entries fold into that node's
24	overflow entry.
25	
26	Persistence is multi-revision, incremental and crash safe. Each ``save``
27	is a commit serialized through a lock file inside the lens directory: it
28	folds the records folded since the last load or save into the schema of
29	the newest committed revision and writes the result as one brand new,
30	complete revision file in the ``versions`` directory, each revision
31	carrying its own monotonic number and checksum. Revision files are never
32	rewritten; a new revision only appears by an atomic rename of a fully
33	synced file and its number is one greater than the previous newest, so
34	readers see a total order and old revisions are pruned once more than
35	``max_versions`` complete revisions exist. A crash or an interrupted
36	commit can therefore only ever leave complete revisions, and any reader
37	observes either the previous complete revision or the next one, never a
38	half-written schema. A revision is
39	parsed, structurally validated and checksummed completely before any of
40	its content is handed out; a missing or corrupt requested revision raises
41	``SchemaConflict`` and leaves every other revision usable.
42	
43	``check`` and ``schema`` can either target an explicit revision number or
44	read the snapshot the lens was opened (``load``-ed) at; inference keeps
45	appending batches as before. ``versions`` lists the committed revisions
46	oldest first and ``rollback`` expresses the target revision's schema as a
47	brand new commit, so history is appended to and never rewritten. A
48	revision that has already been pruned (or never existed) makes a rollback
49	raise ``SchemaConflict`` without touching any committed revision.
50	
51	A lens directory holding only the old single-file format (``schema.json``)
52	is still read; the legacy file is migrated in place into the revisions
53	layout on first read, and a failed migration leaves the original file and
54	the in-memory schema untouched and raises ``SchemaConflict`` so it can be
55	retried later.
56	
57	The oldest segment of the history can be compacted into one baseline
58	version. A baseline file carries the schema and statistics exactly as they
59	stood at the end of the merged range (the folded tree is checked
60	field-for-field against the last merged revision before the switch), and a
61	small manifest in the versions directory is the single pointer naming at
62	most one baseline file. Compaction stages a temp artifact, validates it
63	fully, only then atomically replaces the manifest, and deletes no merged
64	input until that switch has landed; a crash mid-compaction is reconciled
65	into "completely happened" or "never happened" the next time the lock is
66	taken. Reads never wait on a compaction: while it runs they route through
67	the old manifest to complete revisions, and afterwards the baseline is
68	readable as its anchor revision while the revisions merged into it answer
69	``SchemaConflict``.
70	"""
71	
72	from __future__ import annotations
73	
74	import contextlib
75	import copy
76	import hashlib
77	import itertools
78	import json
79	import os
80	import threading
81	import time
82	from pathlib import Path
83	from typing import Any, Iterable, Iterator
84	
85	try:
86	    import fcntl
87	except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - Windows
88	    fcntl = None  # type: ignore[assignment]
89	try:
90	    import msvcrt
91	except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - Windows
92	    msvcrt = None  # type: ignore[assignment]
93	
94	SCHEMA_FILENAME = "schema.json"
95	LOCK_FILENAME = "schema.lock"
96	VERSIONS_DIRNAME = "versions"
97	REVISION_PREFIX = "revision-"
98	REVISION_SUFFIX = ".json"
99	BASELINE_PREFIX = "baseline-"
100	BASELINE_SUFFIX = ".json"
101	MANIFEST_FILENAME = "manifest.json"
102	DEFAULT_MAX_VERSIONS = 10
103	DEFAULT_COMPACT_KEEP = 5
104	SCHEMA_VERSION = 3
105	# Version 1 files predate approximation markers; version 2 is the single
106	# file layout. All three encodings carry the same node tree, so legacy
107	# files migrate to the revisions layout without re-interpreting the tree.
108	READABLE_VERSIONS = (1, 2, SCHEMA_VERSION)
109	# The overflow entry marks approximated locations in stats paths. It is a
110	# key no JSON object can literally carry, so it can never collide with a
111	# real field name (a field literally named "*" stays locatable as
112	# ``$["*"]`` while the marker renders as ``$.*``).
113	OVERFLOW_MARKER = "*\x00*"
114	
115	# Each compaction attempt stages its artifact under a unique temp name;
116	# the file only takes its final baseline name by an atomic rename taken
117	# under the commit lock, so concurrent compactions never overwrite each
118	# other's staging file and a retried switch can never unlink a baseline a
119	# winning switch already committed.
120	_STAGING_COUNTER = itertools.count()
121	
122	
123	def _staging_name() -> str:
124	    return f"staging-{os.getpid()}-{next(_STAGING_COUNTER)}.tmp"
125	
126	
127	def _write_staging(directory: Path, text: str) -> Path:
128	    """Write a uniquely named, fully synced staging file in ``directory``."""
129	    for _ in range(100):
130	        path = directory / _staging_name()
131	        try:
132	            fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o644)
133	        except FileExistsError:
134	            continue
135	        try:
136	            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
137	                handle.write(text)
138	                handle.flush()
139	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
140	        except BaseException:
141	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
142	                os.unlink(path)
143	            raise
144	        return path
145	    raise SchemaConflict("cannot allocate a compaction staging file")
146	
147	_KINDS = ("null", "boolean", "number", "string", "array", "object")
148	
149	
150	class SchemaConflict(Exception):
151	    """Raised when an operation conflicts with the stored schema state."""
152	
153	
154	class _RevisionMissing(SchemaConflict):
155	    """Internal: a mapped revision/baseline file is not on disk (a race)."""
156	
157	
158	def _kind_of(value: Any) -> str:
159	    if value is None:
160	        return "null"
161	    if isinstance(value, bool):
162	        return "boolean"
163	    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
164	        return "number"
165	    if isinstance(value, str):
166	        return "string"
167	    if isinstance(value, list):
168	        return "array"
169	    if isinstance(value, dict):
170	        return "object"
171	    raise ValueError(f"unsupported value type: {type(value).__name__}")
172	
173	
174	def _new_node(kind: str) -> dict:
175	    node: dict[str, Any] = {"kind": kind}
176	    if kind == "object":
177	        node["fields"] = {}
178	        node["count"] = 0
179	    elif kind == "array":
180	        node["elements"] = {}
181	    return node
182	
183	
184	def _collapsed_node(kind: str) -> dict:
185	    """A depth-capped node: marked approximate, sub-structure not tracked.
186	
187	    Collapsed objects keep only a record count; collapsed arrays keep only
188	    the kinds of their elements (each of which is itself collapsed or a
189	    scalar), so the memory a collapsed subtree can use is bounded.
190	    """
191	    node: dict[str, Any] = {"kind": kind, "approximate": True}
192	    if kind == "object":
193	        node["count"] = 0
194	    elif kind == "array":
195	        node["elements"] = {}
196	    return node
197	
198	
199	def _is_collapsed(node: dict) -> bool:
200	    """Whether an object node is a depth-capped summary without fields."""
201	    return (
202	        node["kind"] == "object"
203	        and bool(node.get("approximate"))
204	        and "fields" not in node
205	    )
206	
207	
208	def _new_field() -> dict:
209	    return {"types": {}, "observed": 0, "total": 0, "optional": False}
210	
211	
212	def _overflow_add_name(entry: dict, name: str) -> None:
213	    """Record that ``name`` really folded into an overflow entry.
214	
215	    The list is kept sorted (and de-duplicated) so the schema tree stays
216	    canonical across folds, commits and reloads. An explicit ``names:
217	    None`` marks a pre-tracking overflow entry whose provenance is
218	    unknown; adding a known name cannot narrow that, so it stays unknown.
219	    """
220	    if "names" in entry and entry["names"] is None:
221	        return
222	    names = entry.setdefault("names", [])
223	    if name not in names:
224	        names.append(name)
225	        names.sort()
226	
227	
228	def _union_overflow_names(left: dict | None, right: dict | None) -> list[str] | None:
229	    """Union the folded-name provenance of two entries.
230	
231	    A normal exact entry carries no ``names`` key (empty provenance); an
232	    explicit ``names: None`` marks an overflow entry loaded from a file
233	    written before provenance was tracked, whose folded names are unknown
234	    and must keep widening for every name.
235	    """
236	    if left is None or right is None:
237	        return None
238	
239	    def provenance(entry: dict) -> list[str] | None:
240	        if "names" not in entry:
241	            return []
242	        return entry["names"]
243	
244	    ln = provenance(left)
245	    rn = provenance(right)
246	    if ln is None or rn is None:
247	        return None
248	    return sorted(set(ln) | set(rn))
249	
250	
251	def _fold_object(
252	    node: dict,
253	    record: dict,
254	    depth: int = 0,
255	    max_fields: int | None = None,
256	    max_depth: int | None = None,
257	) -> None:
258	    if _is_collapsed(node):
259	        node["count"] += 1
260	        return
261	    node["count"] += 1
262	    fields = node["fields"]
263	    overflow = node.get("overflow")
264	    for name, value in record.items():
265	        entry = fields.get(name)
266	        if entry is None:
267	            if max_fields is not None and len(fields) >= max_fields:
268	                # The field cap is reached: fold this and every further new
269	                # name into the shared overflow entry. The entry is marked
270	                # approximate; its type set only widens and its observation

279	                continue

281	            fields[name] = entry

283	        _fold_value(entry["types"], value, depth + 1, max_fields, max_depth)

329	def _cap_object_fields(node: dict, max_fields: int | None) -> None:
330	    """Fold exact fields beyond the cap into the overflow entry.
331	
332	    Applied recursively after two batches merge: folding each batch under
333	    the cap bounds the names it introduces, but disjoint names across
334	    batches could otherwise leave a merged node with up to twice the cap
335	    exact entries. Entries are folded in name order, so which names stay
336	    exact is deterministic; folded entries widen the existing overflow
337	    entry (which may itself carry records seen under names neither batch
338	    tracked exactly) and the result is marked approximate.
339	    """
340	    if _is_collapsed(node):
341	        return
342	    if max_fields is not None and len(node["fields"]) > max_fields:
343	        # Keep the first names tracked exactly and fold the rest; merged
344	        # field order follows global first-seen order (left batch then
345	        # names new in the right batch), so this lands on exactly the
346	        # entries a single capped pass over every record would have kept.
347	        names = list(node["fields"])
348	        excess = names[max_fields:]
349	        fields = node["fields"]
350	        overflow = node.get("overflow")
351	        for name in excess:
352	            entry = fields.pop(name)
353	            overflow = (
354	                _merge_field(overflow, entry)
355	                if overflow is not None
356	                else copy.deepcopy(entry)
357	            )
358	            # The popped entry was an exact field at this node; its name is
359	            # the provenance it adds to the node's overflow. Overflow
360	            # provenance deeper in its type tree rides along in the merge.
361	            _overflow_add_name(overflow, name)
362	            overflow["approximate"] = True
363	            node["overflow"] = overflow
364	    for entry in node["fields"].values():
365	        for child in entry["types"].values():
366	            _cap_node_fields(child, max_fields)
367	    overflow = node.get("overflow")
368	    if overflow is not None:
369	        for child in overflow["types"].values():
370	            _cap_node_fields(child, max_fields)
371

374	    if node["kind"] == "object":
375	        _cap_object_fields(node, max_fields)
376	    elif node["kind"] == "array":
377	        for child in node["elements"].values():
378	            _cap_node_fields(child, max_fields)

381	def _merge_node(left: dict, right: dict) -> dict:
382	    """Fold two schema nodes over disjoint batches into one new node."""
383	    kind = left["kind"]
384	    if kind == "object":
385	        if _is_collapsed(left) or _is_collapsed(right):
386	            # One side gave up per-field detail, so the union can only be
387	            # reported as a collapsed, marked summary.
388	            node = _collapsed_node("object")
389	            node["count"] = left["count"] + right["count"]
390	            return node
391	        node = _new_node("object")
392	        node["count"] = left["count"] + right["count"]
393	        left_overflow = left.get("overflow")
394	        right_overflow = right.get("overflow")
395	        names = list(left["fields"]) + [
396	            name for name in right["fields"] if name not in left["fields"]
397	        ]
398	        for name in names:
399	            le = left["fields"].get(name)
400	            re = right["fields"].get(name)
401	            if le is None:
402	                # The field is missing on the left; if the left capped its
403	                # fields, its occurrences of this field landed in the left
404	                # overflow entry, so the merged entry must absorb them and
405	                # be marked approximate. That field's own occurrences on
406	                # the right prove its name is folded too.
407	                if left_overflow is not None:
408	                    entry = _merge_field(left_overflow, re)
409	                    _overflow_add_name(entry, name)
410	                    entry["approximate"] = True
411	                else:
412	                    entry = copy.deepcopy(re)
413	            elif re is None:
414	                if right_overflow is not None:
415	                    entry = _merge_field(le, right_overflow)
416	                    _overflow_add_name(entry, name)
417	                    entry["approximate"] = True
418	                else:
419	                    entry = copy.deepcopy(le)
420	            else:
421	                entry = _merge_field(le, re)
422	            node["fields"][name] = entry
423	        if left_overflow is not None or right_overflow is not None:
424	            if left_overflow is None:
425	                overflow = copy.deepcopy(right_overflow)
426	            elif right_overflow is None:
427	                overflow = copy.deepcopy(left_overflow)
428	            else:
429	                overflow = _merge_field(left_overflow, right_overflow)
430	            overflow["approximate"] = True
431	            node["overflow"] = overflow
432	        return node
433	    if kind == "array":
434	        node = _new_node("array")
435	        if left.get("approximate") or right.get("approximate"):
436	            node["approximate"] = True
437	        kinds = list(left["elements"]) + [
438	            element_kind
439	            for element_kind in right["elements"]
440	            if element_kind not in left["elements"]
441	        ]
442	        for element_kind in kinds:
443	            lc = left["elements"].get(element_kind)
444	            rc = right["elements"].get(element_kind)
445	            if lc is None:
446	                node["elements"][element_kind] = copy.deepcopy(rc)
447	            elif rc is None:
448	                node["elements"][element_kind] = copy.deepcopy(lc)
449	            else:
450	                node["elements"][element_kind] = _merge_node(lc, rc)
451	        return node
452	    return _new_node(kind)

455	def _merge_field(left: dict, right: dict) -> dict:
456	    """Fold two field entries over disjoint batches into one new entry."""
457	    entry = _new_field()
458	    entry["observed"] = left["observed"] + right["observed"]
459	    if left.get("approximate") or right.get("approximate"):
460	        entry["approximate"] = True
461	    # Only overflow-ish entries carry provenance; attaching an empty list
462	    # to ordinary exact entries would make the merged tree differ from a
463	    # single one-shot fold over the same records.
464	    if "names" in left or "names" in right:
465	        entry["names"] = _union_overflow_names(left, right)
466	    kinds = list(left["types"]) + [
467	        kind for kind in right["types"] if kind not in left["types"]
468	    ]
469	    for kind in kinds:
470	        lc = left["types"].get(kind)
471	        rc = right["types"].get(kind)
472	        if lc is None:
473	            entry["types"][kind] = copy.deepcopy(rc)
474	        elif rc is None:
475	            entry["types"][kind] = copy.deepcopy(lc)
476	        else:
477	            entry["types"][kind] = _merge_node(lc, rc)
478	    return entry

481	def _subtract_node(mem: dict, base: dict) -> dict:
482	    """Return the part of ``mem`` folded after ``base`` was taken."""
483	    kind = mem["kind"]
484	    if kind == "object":
485	        if _is_collapsed(mem):
486	            node = _collapsed_node("object")
487	            node["count"] = mem["count"] - base.get("count", 0)
488	            return node
489	        node = _new_node("object")
490	        node["count"] = mem["count"] - base.get("count", 0)
491	        base_fields = base.get("fields") or {}
492	        for name, entry in mem["fields"].items():
493	            base_entry = base_fields.get(name)
494	            if base_entry is None:
495	                node["fields"][name] = copy.deepcopy(entry)
496	            else:
497	                node["fields"][name] = _subtract_field(entry, base_entry)
498	        mem_overflow = mem.get("overflow")
499	        if mem_overflow is not None:
500	            base_overflow = base.get("overflow")
501	            if base_overflow is None:
502	                node["overflow"] = copy.deepcopy(mem_overflow)
503	            else:
504	                node["overflow"] = _subtract_field(mem_overflow, base_overflow)
505	        return node
506	    if kind == "array":
507	        node = _new_node("array")
508	        if mem.get("approximate"):
509	            node["approximate"] = True
510	        base_elements = base.get("elements") or {}
511	        for element_kind, child in mem["elements"].items():
512	            base_child = base_elements.get(element_kind)
513	            if base_child is None:
514	                node["elements"][element_kind] = copy.deepcopy(child)
515	            else:
516	                node["elements"][element_kind] = _subtract_node(child, base_child)
517	        return node
518	    return _new_node(kind)

521	def _subtract_field(mem: dict, base: dict) -> dict:
522	    entry = _new_field()
523	    entry["observed"] = mem["observed"] - base["observed"]
524	    if mem.get("approximate"):
525	        entry["approximate"] = True
526	    mem_names = mem.get("names")
527	    if mem_names is not None:
528	        # The delta cannot attribute provenance per name (only aggregate
529	        # counts are kept), so it carries every name its memory ever folded
530	        # in; the downstream merge is a union anyway, and over-inclusion
531	        # only ever widens validation for genuinely folded names.
532	        entry["names"] = sorted(mem_names)
533	    for kind, child in mem["types"].items():
534	        base_child = base["types"].get(kind)
535	        if base_child is None:
536	            entry["types"][kind] = copy.deepcopy(child)
537	        else:
538	            entry["types"][kind] = _subtract_node(child, base_child)
539	    return entry

542	def _join(path: str, name: str) -> str:
543	    # An identifier is joined with a dot; every other key is quoted in
544	    # brackets so a name containing a dot or a backslash can never be read
545	    # as a path separator: $["a.b"] is distinct from $.a.b.
546	    if name.isidentifier():

553	
554	    The marker can never be a real key (see ``OVERFLOW_MARKER``), so a bare
555	    ``.*`` segment cannot be produced by ``_join`` for any real field name;
556	    a field literally named "*" quotes as ``$["*"]`` and stays distinct.

561	def _check_object(node: dict, record: dict, path: str, reports: list[str]) -> None:
562	    if _is_collapsed(node):
563	        # A depth-capped node tracked no fields, so nothing inside the
564	        # record's value can be checked; the approximation is marked in
565	        # the schema instead of guessed about here.
566	        return
567	    fields = node["fields"]
568	    overflow = node.get("overflow")
569	    overflow_names = None if overflow is None else overflow.get("names")
570	    for name in record:
571	        if name not in fields:
572	            if overflow is not None and (
573	                overflow_names is None or name in overflow_names
574	            ):
575	                # Only names that really folded into the overflow entry are
576	                # checked against its widened type set; ``names is None``
577	                # marks a legacy overflow entry with unknown provenance. A
578	                # name never seen before is still unexpected.
579	                _check_value(overflow["types"], record[name], _join(path, name), reports)
580	            else:
581	                reports.append(f"{_join(path, name)}: unexpected field")
582	    for name, entry in fields.items():
583	        if name not in record:
584	            if not entry["optional"]:
585	                reports.append(f"{_join(path, name)}: missing required field")
586	            continue
587	        _check_value(entry["types"], record[name], _join(path, name), reports)

590	def _check_value(types: dict, value: Any, path: str, reports: list[str]) -> None:
591	    kind = _kind_of(value)
592	    node = types.get(kind)
593	    if node is None:
594	        expected = ", ".join(sorted(types))
595	        reports.append(f"{path}: type {kind} not in field types [{expected}]")
596	        return
597	    if kind == "object":
598	        _check_object(node, value, path, reports)
599	    elif kind == "array":
600	        for index, element in enumerate(value):
601	            _check_value(node["elements"], element, f"{path}[{index}]", reports)

604	def _normalize_overflow_names(node: Any) -> None:
605	    """Mark pre-tracking overflow entries with explicit ``names: None``.
606	
607	    Files written before folded names were tracked carry overflow entries
608	    without a ``names`` key; unlike an exact entry (which also omits the
609	    key), their provenance is unknown and must stay permissive through
610	    merges. Exact entries are never reached here.
611	    """
612	    if not isinstance(node, dict):
613	        return
614	    kind = node.get("kind")
615	    if kind == "object" and not _is_collapsed(node):
616	        overflow = node.get("overflow")
617	        if overflow is not None and "names" not in overflow:
618	            overflow["names"] = None
619	        fields = node.get("fields") or {}
620	        for entry in fields.values():
621	            for child in (entry.get("types") or {}).values():
622	                _normalize_overflow_names(child)
623	        if overflow is not None:
624	            for child in (overflow.get("types") or {}).values():
625	                _normalize_overflow_names(child)
626	    elif kind == "array":
627	        for child in (node.get("elements") or {}).values():
628	            _normalize_overflow_names(child)

631	def _validate_node(node: Any) -> None:
632	    if not isinstance(node, dict) or node.get("kind") not in _KINDS:
633	        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: malformed node")
634	    approximate = node.get("approximate", False)
635	    if not isinstance(approximate, bool):
636	        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: malformed node")
637	    kind = node["kind"]
638	    if kind == "object":
639	        fields = node.get("fields")
640	        count = node.get("count")
641	        if isinstance(count, bool) or not isinstance(count, int):
642	            raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: malformed object node")
643	        if fields is None:
644	            # Only a collapsed (approximate) object node may omit fields.
645	            if not approximate:
646	                raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: malformed object node")
647	            fields = {}
648	        if not isinstance(fields, dict):
649	            raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: malformed object node")
650	        for entry in fields.values():
651	            _validate_field(entry)
652	        overflow = node.get("overflow")
653	        if overflow is not None:
654	            _validate_field(overflow)
655	    elif kind == "array":
656	        elements = node.get("elements")
657	        if not isinstance(elements, dict):
658	            raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: malformed array node")
659	        for child in elements.values():
660	            _validate_node(child)

667	    observed = entry.get("observed")
668	    total = entry.get("total")
669	    optional = entry.get("optional")
670	    approximate = entry.get("approximate", False)
671	    names = entry.get("names")
672	    if (
673	        not isinstance(types, dict)
674	        or isinstance(observed, bool)
675	        or not isinstance(observed, int)
676	        or isinstance(total, bool)
677	        or not isinstance(total, int)

685	            )
686	        )

693	def _checksum(root: dict) -> str:
694	    """Checksum of the whole schema in its canonical JSON encoding."""
695	    canonical = json.dumps(root, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
696	    return hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

699	def _validate_payload(payload: Any) -> tuple[int, dict]:
700	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
701	        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: not a JSON object")
702	    version = payload.get("version")
703	    if version not in READABLE_VERSIONS:
704	        raise SchemaConflict(f"unsupported schema version: {version!r}")
705	    checksum = payload.get("checksum")
706	    if not isinstance(checksum, str):
707	        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: missing checksum")
708	    if "root" not in payload:
709	        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: missing root")
710	    root = payload["root"]
711	    _validate_node(root)
712	    if not isinstance(root, dict) or root.get("kind") != "object":
713	        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: root must be an object")
714	    if _checksum(root) != checksum:
715	        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: checksum mismatch")
716	    _normalize_overflow_names(root)
717	    return version, root

733	def _write_atomic(file_path: Path, text: str) -> None:
734	    """Write text atomically: a crash leaves only the old or new file."""
735	    tmp = file_path.with_name(file_path.name + ".tmp")
736	    fd = os.open(tmp, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o644)
737	    try:
738	        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
739	            handle.write(text)
740	            handle.flush()
741	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
742	        os.replace(tmp, file_path)
743	    except BaseException:
744	        try:
745	            os.unlink(tmp)
746	        except OSError:
747	            pass
748	        raise
749	    _fsync_dir(file_path.parent)
